# 1 Kings Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into the City of David until he had finished building his own house and the house of the LORD and the wall around Jerusalem.
**2** The people, however, were sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD.
**3** Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
**4** The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
**5** At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night. And God said, "Ask what I shall give you."
**6** Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart toward you. And you have kept for him this great loyal love and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
**7** And now, O LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father. But I am a young child; I do not know how to go out or come in.
**8** Your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, a great people, too numerous to be numbered or counted.
**9** Give your servant therefore a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of yours?"
**10** The request pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
**11** God said to him, "Because you have asked this, and have not asked for yourself long life, nor asked for yourself riches, nor asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice —
**12** behold, I have done according to your words. Behold, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has been before you, and none like you shall arise after you.
**13** I have also given you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that no king shall compare with you all your days.
**14** And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days."
**15** Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
**16** Then two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
**17** The one woman said, "O my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth to a child while she was in the house.
**18** On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no one else with us in the house — only the two of us.
**19** This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.
**20** She arose at midnight and took my son from beside me while your servant slept, and laid him at her breast, and laid her dead son at my breast.
**21** When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, behold, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, behold, he was not the son I had borne."
**22** The other woman said, "No, the living son is mine, and the dead son is yours." The first said, "No, the dead son is yours, and the living son is mine." Thus they spoke before the king.
**23** Then the king said, "The one says, 'This is my son that is alive, and your son is dead,' while the other says, 'No, your son is dead, and my son is the living one.'"
**24** And the king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword before the king.
**25** The king said, "Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one and half to the other."
**26** Then the woman whose son was alive said to the king — for her heart yearned for her son — "O my lord, give her the living child, and by no means put him to death." But the other said, "He shall be neither mine nor yours; divide him."
**27** Then the king answered and said, "Give the living child to the first woman, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother."
**28** All Israel heard of the judgment that the king had rendered, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to execute justice.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

**Key Observations**:
- EMET preserves Hebrew word order and particles (ʾet, vav-consecutive) that reveal syntactic emphasis
- LOGOS provides the most balanced English rendering suitable for study
- PNEUMA's dynamic approach often captures emotional register and narrative pacing most effectively

- **LOGOS**: Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart toward you. And you have kep...
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon replied, "You showed tremendous faithful love to your servant, my father David, because he lived before you with integrity, righteousness, and an honest heart. And you have continued this grea...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 7
- **EMET**: And-now, YHWH my-God, you have-made-king ʾet-your-servant in-place-of David my-father. And-I am a-small youth; I-do-not know going-out or-coming-in.
- **LOGOS**: And now, O LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father. But I am a young child; I do not know how to go out or come in.
- **PNEUMA**: Now, LORD my God, you have made me king in my father's place. But I am practically a child — I don't know the first thing about leading.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **PNEUMA**: And here I am, surrounded by your chosen people — a nation so vast it cannot be counted.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **LOGOS**: Give your servant therefore a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of yours?"
- **PNEUMA**: So give me a heart that listens — one that can govern your people and tell right from wrong. For who could possibly govern this great people of yours?"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **EMET**: And-also what you-did-not ask I-have-given to-you, both riches and-honor, so-that there-shall-not-be a-man like-you among-the-kings all your-days.
- **LOGOS**: I have also given you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that no king shall compare with you all your days.
- **PNEUMA**: And I am also giving you what you did not ask for — wealth and honor beyond any king of your time.

- **PNEUMA**: And if you walk in my ways and obey my commands as your father David did, I will also give you a long life."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **EMET**: And-Solomon awoke, and-behold — a-dream. And-he-came to-Jerusalem and-stood before the-ark-of the-covenant-of the-Lord, and-offered-up burnt-offerings and-made peace-offerings, and-made a-feast for-al...
- **LOGOS**: Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his serva...

- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 16
- **EMET**: Then two women, prostitutes, came to the-king, and-stood before-him.
- **LOGOS**: Then two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
- **PNEUMA**: Some time later, two prostitutes came before the king.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 18
- **EMET**: And-it-was on-the-third day after-my-giving-birth, and-this woman also gave-birth. And-we were together; there-was-no stranger with-us in-the-house — only the-two-of-us in-the-house.
- **LOGOS**: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no one else with us in the house — only the two of us.
- **PNEUMA**: Three days later, she also had a baby. We were alone — no one else was in the house, just the two of us.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

- **LOGOS**: This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.

- **LOGOS**: She arose at midnight and took my son from beside me while your servant slept, and laid him at her breast, and laid her dead son at my breast.

### Verse 27
- **EMET**: And-the-king answered and-said, "Give to-her ʾet-the-living newborn, and-dying do-not kill-him. She is his-mother."
- **LOGOS**: Then the king answered and said, "Give the living child to the first woman, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother."
- **PNEUMA**: Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is the mother."

### Verse 28
- **EMET**: And-all Israel heard ʾet-the-judgment that the-king had-judged, and-they-feared before the-king, for they-saw that the-wisdom-of God was in-him to-do justice.
